overview_markdown:
ESP-Claw is Espressif's official **Chat Coding** AI agent framework for IoT devices, explicitly inspired by the OpenClaw concept and reimplemented in C on top of ESP-IDF. It runs the full agent loop — sensing, decision-making, and execution — locally on ESP32-series chips costing only a few dollars, turning traditionally passive IoT endpoints into active decision-making centers.

Its standout architecture combines IM-style chat interaction with dynamic Lua module loading, letting ordinary users define and update device behavior conversationally without writing firmware. An event-driven runtime allows any hardware or network event to trigger the agent loop with millisecond-level response, and recent commits show active maintenance around CLI stability, flashing tools, Lua module APIs, and a newly added security policy.

Compared to OpenClaw, which targets desktops and servers with large-context models, ESP-Claw trades reasoning depth and ecosystem breadth for extreme footprint efficiency and true edge autonomy. It is best viewed as the embedded frontier of the OpenClaw idea rather than a feature-equivalent alternative.
